chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammat and Salih ibn Sa'id, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

— that he was asked a question and he answered regarding it. Then the man said: 'The jurists do not say this!' So he said: 'O woe unto you! Have you ever seen a jurist at all? Verily, the jurist who is truly a jurist is the one ascetic in this world, desirous of the Hereafter, and holding fast to the Sunnah of the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.زاهد: ascetic, one who abstains from worldly attractions
key_terms.سنة النبي: the Prophetic Sunnah, the practice and tradition of the Prophet
key_terms.فقيه: jurist, one who has deep understanding of Islamic law (fiqh)
key_terms.متمسك: one who holds fast, one who clings firmly

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a true faqih (jurist) according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) defines the true faqih (Islamic jurist) as one who combines three qualities: asceticism in worldly matters, earnest desire for the Hereafter, and firm adherence to the Prophetic Sunnah. When a man challenged the Imam's juristic ruling by appealing to the authority of contemporary jurists, the Imam responded with this rhetorical question, implying that the so-called jurists of his time did not embody true Islamic scholarship. This teaching reflects the Shia understanding that genuine religious authority (fiqh) cannot be separated from spiritual and moral rectitude.
